title: Indo Farm Equipment Ltd - 544328 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue rose 2.73% YoY to ₹128.58 crore while FY27 guidance calls for 20–25% revenue growth and ~12.5% operating EBITDA margin.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 standalone revenue was ₹128.58 crore (up 2.73% YoY, up 27.77% QoQ) and EBITDA was ₹17.47 crore (up 0.57% YoY). FY26 turnover grew 14.39% to ₹419.54 crore, with tractors up 42.85% to ₹201.45 crore and cranes down about 3% to ₹218.09 crore. Management attributed the crane weakness to the Term III to Term V emission norm shift and steel cost spikes, and said pass-through is now complete. The new Bhud (Himachal Pradesh) pick-and-carry crane plant and a tower crane line are guided to start commercial production in Q2 FY27, after repeated delays. Several answers on order book, cash flow and the NBFC provisioning were vague or deferred to email.

financial_highlights.change: down from prior periods per analyst

segments.name: Tractors
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue ₹201.45 crore (+42.85%) on 3,006 units; FY27 guided to grow 25–30%. Steady-state EBIT margin guided at about 10%. Consolidated tractor profit fell to ₹410 lakh vs ₹631 lakh standalone, attributed to NBFC NPA-norm provisioning.

segments.name: Cranes (pick-and-carry, existing plant)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue ₹218.09 crore (about -3%) on 1,003 units; existing plant utilisation about 80%+ in FY26 vs 90%+ in FY25. FY27 guided to grow 15–20%. Q4 margin fell to about 10.4%, attributed to emission-norm cost pass-through and steel inflation.

segments.name: Tower cranes (new)
segments.commentary: Trials complete; commercial production targeted Q2 FY27. Small order book in single digits, all from north India, with ASP guided at ₹60–70 lakh (range ₹40 lakh to ₹75–80 lakh). Management guided 60–80 machines over the next six months, with 50–60% utilisation in year one.

guidance_outlook: FY27 overall revenue growth of about 20–25%; tractors 25–30%; existing crane plant 15–20%.
FY27 operating EBITDA margin guided at about 12.5% vs about 13% in FY26, with pressure from new products and markets.
New Bhud pick-and-carry plant to start commercial production in Q2 FY27; about 30–35% utilisation in first six months, 500–600 units minimum from that point.
Full utilisation of new pick-and-carry and tower crane capacity expected by FY28–29; 70–80% crane plant utilisation by FY29–30.
Other costs expected to settle at about 11–12% of revenue; working capital days to come under 200 by FY28–29 from about 307 days.
Internal plan of about 25% average annual growth until existing capacity is fully used.
capex_capacity: Total capex for new crane project about ₹70-plus crore, of which about ₹25 crore spent to date; balance to be spent in FY27.
Tower crane capacity of 240–250 machines per year initially, expandable without more capex (only welding machines to add).
Combined crane capacity after new plant cited as about 5,000 units (existing about 1,200 plus about 3,600 additional).
Existing tractor plant utilisation about 35% on reported volumes; management suggested 40–45% when including transmission supplied to cranes.
Bhud site: main shed steel nearly complete, pre-engineered building expected by July 2026; machine orders placed.
demand_pricing: Crane market size estimated at about 12,000–14,000 pick-and-carry units last year (management estimate, no public association data).
Company currently operates in less than half of India for cranes; crane dealer network 25+ and tractor dealer network 225+ after adding 23 in Q4.
Tractor FY26 growth was helped by a one-time custom hiring order from a southern state; export business in Nepal and Myanmar has weakened.
Export: a trial order of about 48 tractors from a German company worth about ₹6 crore; FY26 export about ₹21 crore.
About 20%+ of tractor sales financed through captive NBFC Barota; retail financing availability cited as a past constraint.
Tower crane competition is a two-player market (one foreign at 25–30% higher pricing, one Indian).

qa_highlights.question: Why did tractor volumes stay around 3,000 vs 4,500 in FY22, and why did margins decline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY22 included a one-time southern custom hiring order and Nepal/Myanmar exports that have since weakened; retail financing constraints also held back volumes. Captive NBFC investment and financier support are expected to drive growth in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Why is crane margin down in Q4 and what is driving it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the drop to the emission-norm upgrade cost, only partly passed on earlier, plus a sharp steel price rise in Q4. Management says full pass-through is now done and the market will accept it from the next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the crane capacity commissioning delayed and why are dealers flat?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited Himachal monsoon delays, sand mining permission hurdles, and gas/commodity supply problems after the Middle East situation. It said the delay is not deliberate and it is confident of the planned numbers once the market is opened.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for other costs and the working capital cycle?
qa_highlights.answer: Other costs rose from ₹56 crore to ₹64 crore on freight, discounts and promotions and are guided to 11–12% of revenue. Working capital days, now about 307, are expected to fall below 200 by FY28–29 as volumes rise.

qa_highlights.question: What is the tower crane order book and margin outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is a small order book in single digits, all from north India, with deliveries starting Q2. Margins are expected to be similar to pick-and-carry cranes, and initial margins will be low.

qa_highlights.question: What is the executable order book and export contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no long-term order book; dealers replenish stock monthly, with some corporate and government orders (such as one from NTPC) on 60–90 day terms. Export was about ₹21 crore last year and a German trial order of about ₹6 crore has been received.

risks_watch: Crane plant commissioning has slipped repeatedly (October, then March, then Q2 FY27); fund utilisation about 73% as of March, with funds parked in FDRs.
FY27 EBITDA margin guided down to about 12.5% from about 13%, with the new products and markets adding pressure.
Crane dealer count was flat quarter-on-quarter at 25+ per the analyst, and management has not yet shown tower crane deliveries.
Market oversupply risk: new capacity of about 3,600 units is roughly 25–30% of the estimated 12,000–14,000 unit pick-and-carry market.
Consolidated cash flow fell from about ₹53 crore to about ₹30 crore; management deferred the explanation to email.
NBFC NPA-norm change requires higher provisioning, reducing consolidated tractor profit.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the long-term plan and capacity additions, but cautious and evasive on near-term specifics. Management deferred the cash flow, R&D and product-expansion questions, and gave loose or inconsistent answers on the crane timeline, tower crane margin and order book.
key_quotes: Ma'am, that new project has not yet started. Once the new project starts, then only the number will come.
So, for the past four years, we have been working at 100% capacity of our old plant.
We will explain it to you, I think you can mail us, and I can check up with my CFO.

growth.why: FY27 revenue guided at 20-25% (midpoint 22.5%), with tractors +25-30% and existing cranes +15-20%; backing is partial, with the Bhud plant (₹70+ cr capex, ~₹25 cr spent, start Q2 FY27) and 60-80 tower crane orders over six months, but order book and cash-flow answers were vague and the new plant has slipped before.
